extracted.intended_audience: federal policymakers, National Academy of Sciences, university administrators, and program designers for national science talent development
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and measurable standards for discovering and developing scientific talent in American youth via scholarships, fellowships, selection procedures, obligations, and near-term remedies for wartime deficits in scientific personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale of scholarship awards
rubrics_metrics.description: We recommend that each year 6,000 4-year scholarships be awarded, to enable youth of scientific promise to work for bachelor’s degrees in scientific and technological fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum total of Scholars, if and when the plan is in full operation, would be 24,000. Quotas to be prorated to States based on prior-year secondary school graduates. Scholars should be chosen solely on the basis of merit and be eligible for subsequent fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale of fellowship awards
rubrics_metrics.description: We recommend that 300 3-year fellowships be awarded each year to enable the recipients to obtain advanced training leading to doctoral degrees in science and technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum total number of Fellows would be 900. Fellows should be chosen by a national committee of selection, be chosen on merit, and be open to Scholars as well as other qualified students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial support levels for Scholars and Fellows
rubrics_metrics.description: For Scholars: scale of support should be that provided by the GI bill of rights — up to $500 annually for tuition and other fees, plus $50 monthly for personal support if single, and $75 monthly if married. For Fellows: allowance up to $500 for tuition and other fees and up to $100 monthly for personal support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum annual costs when fully realized may reach, after the fourth year, $29,000,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of selection and nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scholars and Fellows should be chosen solely on the basis of merit, without regard to sex, color, race, creed, or need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merit should also be the sole basis for continuing to hold scholarships and fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing-eligibility and termination standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the Scholars and Fellows maintain good behavior, good health, and scientific progress in the top quarter of their classes, the assistance they are receiving should be terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarships last 4 years; fellowships maximum of 3 years. Merit, behavior, health, and being in the top quarter academically are explicit continuing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: We recommend that the establishment of the organization to operate the plan and its supervision be entrusted to the National Academy of Sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: NAS is the nation's top scientific organization with demonstrated knowledge, integrity, and ability to withstand pressures — suitable for operating and supervising the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: State and national selection committees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scholars should be chosen by State committees of selection and the Fellows by a national committee of selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The quotas of scholarships to be awarded by the State (and Territorial) committees of selection should be determined by the number of their secondary school graduates of the previous year as related to the national total.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Science Reserve enrollment and obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: All those who receive benefits under this plan, both Scholars and Fellows, should be enrolled in a National Science Reserve and be liable to call into the service of the Federal Government in connection with scientific or technical work in time of war or other national emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation is viewed as a quid pro quo making Federal investment defensible and would speed mobilization of scientific manpower in emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionate-allocation principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for the discovery and development of scientific talent must be related to the other needs of society for high ability; do not draw into science any more of high ability than science’s proportionate share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive scholarships/fellowships that would siphon a disproportionate share of the nation's top ability into science to the detriment of other fields and to science itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate wartime remedies — selection of promising servicemen
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that the Research Board for National Security and the Army and Navy find men who, before induction and during their service, have shown promise of scientific ability and that they be ordered, by name, to duty in the United States as students for training in science and engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merit should be sole basis for selection; probably no more than 100,000 selected; selection should not disrupt discharge plans and should not be left to volunteer requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterans education and counseling
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that the Veterans’ Administration set up an adequate counseling service for those veterans of marked scientific talent and that a complete scientific education at Government expense be provided for a group of them selected on the basis of merit and irrespective of the length of their military service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment of the GI Bill of Rights is recommended so the law becomes an instrument for ameliorating the deficits of scientists resulting from the war and selective-service policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality standard for Army/foreign instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses of study set up abroad for soldiers, including courses in science and technology, must be the best and most up-to-date that can be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army universities abroad should be supplemented by other measures because major institutions (e.g., MIT, Caltech, Ryerson Laboratory) cannot be moved abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of research expenditures — categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenses were divided into professional salaries and direct operating expenses of research. Direct operating expenses included expenditures for equipment, apparatus, technical and research assistance, publishing costs associated with research, field trips, expeditions, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A calculated ratio of direct expenses in relation to professional salaries is used as a comparative metric across institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarks for direct-research-expense-to-salary ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed minimum figure in industrial laboratories or science institutes was about forty cents per dollar of professional salary; typical figures are near one dollar, and in certain cases more than two or three dollars. Typical figures for university departments are about twenty cents per dollar of salary, and often considerably lower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highest university figures (with a few exceptions) approximate the lowest figures for industrial labs — these ratios serve as benchmarks of institutional research support levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation of research assistance and productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: There appeared to be a correlation between the research contributions of a university department and the amount of research assistance made available to its professional workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In institutions less adequately provided with such support there are many men with research ability whose productivity could be significantly increased by provision of more adequate research funds used to diminish heavy teaching loads and to provide essential apparatus and technical assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching-load standards and groupings
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions in the survey fall roughly into two groups: Group A — teaching load relatively light (some staff 2–3 hours/week), many expected to devote more than half their time to research; Group B — often State universities with heavier teaching load averaging around 12 classroom hours/week, staff able to devote about one-quarter of their time to research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineering departments generally have heavier teaching schedules (often ~18 classroom hours/week); medical sciences often concentrate teaching in a 4-month term with the remaining 8 months involving little or no teaching. Teaching loads may vary by rank within departments.
